virals.name: Jack Ellis
virals.hook: SaaS clone wars: Beehiiv clone gets cloned, then released for free.
virals.text: Someone on here clones Beehiv because they think it’s too expensive but then someone else clones that person’s SaaS because they think it’s too expensive. And then someone else clones this new person’s product and releases it for free. I can’t stop laughing.
virals.video_tip: Whiteboard three boxes: clone → clone of clone → free release. 8s.
virals.original_en: Someone on here clones Beehiv because they think it’s too expensive but then someone else clones that person’s SaaS because they think it’s too expensive. And then someone else clones this new person’s product and releases it for free. I can’t stop laughing.
virals.draft_en:
Watch the SaaS clone loop on X:

Someone clones Beehiiv because the bill feels high.
Someone else clones that clone for the same reason.
Then a third person ships the free version.

I keep laughing because the race to zero is the product now.

virals.hook: Net Forge: private project to shipped multiplayer agent game builder.

Shareholders,

For the last few weeks we have been building Net Forge, and this week it went from a private project to something any developer, or any AI agent, can pick up and use.

Here is what that means and why we think it matters.

More and more games start as a sentence https://t.co/4IQXXhoKwr

virals.original_en:
Shareholders,

For the last few weeks we have been building Net Forge, and this week it went from a private project to something any developer, or any AI agent, can pick up and use.

Here is what that means and why we think it matters.

More and more games start as a sentence
virals.draft_en:
Net Forge left private alpha this week.

A developer - or an AI agent - can spin up a multiplayer browser game from a single sentence.

That is the shareholder pitch: games start as prompts, and the harness is now public.

virals.name: Tom Otto
virals.hook: 9 things that kill a SaaS before traction.
virals.text:
Founders, here are 9 things that kill a SaaS before it gets traction:

1. Building for 6 months before showing anyone
2. No landing page while "still building"
3. Pricing too low to sustain support costs
4. Ignoring the first 10 users' feedback
5. Perfecting onboarding nobody's

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
